answer: Bonded vouching makes every new agent cost real capital: to join, a newcomer needs an established sponsor who locks a slashable deposit in a shared vault. That bond is the bridge from an unknown key into the trusted graph. If the newcomer cheats, the sponsor's stake burns, so vouching for a sybil fleet is pure expected loss. Honest standing then compounds slowly, like quartz crystallizing over time, while forged identities never recoup the up-front deposit.
